{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when measured by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "The dataset contains 76,655 trials across 8 mice after filtering for the five specified stimulation paradigms.",
    "Combined stimulation accounts for the majority of trials (48,846, ~63.7%), followed by ICMS Only (11,378, ~14.8%), Dim Visual Only (9,603, ~12.5%), Sham (3,505, ~4.6%), and Bright Visual Only (3,323, ~4.3%).",
    "Overall success rate across all paradigms is 72.9% (SD=44.4%), with mean Time-to-Target of 2.81 seconds (SD=2.08 s).",
    "Path Efficiency averages 0.475 (SD=0.467), indicating substantial variability in directness of navigation paths, with some extreme outliers (max=29.8).",
    "Average Speed across all trials is 12.5 units/s (SD=4.46), ranging from very slow (0.12) to very fast (75.4) movements.",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) averages 0.377 (SD=0.240), with values spanning nearly the full possible range (0.0006 to 1.0), suggesting diverse steering behaviors.",
    "The highly skewed distribution of trials across paradigms (Combined dominates) may limit statistical power for comparing smaller groups like Sham and Bright Visual Only."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Sample size imbalance is extreme: Combined has 14.7× more trials than Bright Visual Only and 13.9× more than Sham, which will affect precision of group comparisons.",
    "Path Efficiency shows exceptionally high variance (SD=0.467, nearly equal to mean) with extreme maximum value (29.8), suggesting non-normal distribution and potential outliers that may differ by paradigm.",
    "Success rate variability (SD=0.444) indicates binary outcome with substantial paradigm-dependent effects likely, given the ~73% overall mean.",
    "Time-to-Target ranges across two orders of magnitude (0.5 to 201 seconds), with high SD/mean ratio (~0.74), suggesting potential paradigm-specific differences in fast versus slow trials.",
    "The rank order of paradigm frequency (Combined > ICMS Only > Dim Visual Only > Sham > Bright Visual Only) does not obviously map to expected sensory enhancement hierarchy, suggesting complex interaction effects."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The dataset captures mouse navigation behavior under five distinct stimulation conditions with substantial trial counts, though heavily unbalanced toward Combined stimulation. The high variability in Path Efficiency and presence of extreme outliers suggests that stimulation paradigm strongly influences navigational strategy—particularly whether mice take direct versus circuitous routes to targets. The near-equal mean and standard deviation for Path Efficiency, combined with extreme maximum values, indicates that some paradigms may induce highly inefficient looping or exploratory behaviors while others promote direct trajectories. The Angular Dispersion metric (steering variability) shows wide-ranging values suggesting that certain stimulation types may stabilize or disrupt heading control. For neural prosthetic applications, the dominance of Combined stimulation trials suggests this multimodal approach is preferred experimentally, but the smaller single-modality groups (especially Sham vs. Bright Visual Only) are critical for isolating the specific contributions of ICMS versus visual feedback to navigation performance.",
  "limitations": [
    "No paradigm-specific descriptive statistics are provided in the overview—only global means and standard deviations are available, preventing direct quantitative comparison of group differences.",
    "Extreme imbalance in trial counts across paradigms (48,846 vs. 3,323) will reduce statistical power for between-group comparisons and may violate assumptions of common parametric tests.",
    "Path Efficiency maximum value (29.8) is biologically implausible for a ratio metric (expected range 0-1), suggesting possible data quality issues or calculation artifacts that may vary by paradigm.",
    "The summary_only data view provides no information about within-mouse effects, learning curves, or trial sequence effects that could confound paradigm comparisons.",
    "No information about task difficulty, target distance, or environmental conditions is available to contextualize performance differences.",
    "Temperature=0.5 and prompt template details suggest this analysis was generated with LLM assistance, but the underlying data generation and preprocessing steps are not fully documented."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Compute paradigm-specific descriptive statistics (mean, median, SD, IQR) and visualization (boxplots or violin plots) for all five performance variables stratified by Stim Paradigm, followed by formal statistical testing appropriate for unbalanced designs (e.g., mixed-effects models with mouse as random effect, or Welch's ANOVA for unequal variances). Specifically examine Path Efficiency distribution for outliers and potential calculation errors, and assess whether the extreme maximum value is concentrated in specific paradigms. Conduct pairwise comparisons with appropriate multiple comparison correction, prioritizing the theoretically critical contrasts: Combined versus single modalities, ICMS Only versus Visual-only conditions, and all stimulated conditions versus Sham to isolate stimulation effects from baseline performance."
}
